Crypto Industry Spent Over $64M, Yet Sherrod Brown Wins Ohio Senate Race as Several Pro-Crypto Republicans Lose Seats According to crypto journalist Eleanor Terrett, Sherrod Brown won the Ohio Senate race despite more than $64 million in crypto industry spending. Pro-crypto Republican Representatives Bryan Steil, Zach Nunn and Ann Wagner lost their seats. Pro-crypto Senator Pete Ricketts won the Nebraska race, while pro-crypto Representative Andy Barr won Kentucky’s Senate seat. Terrett expects Tim Scott to become the ranking Republican on the Senate Banking Committee following the shift in Senate control. The race involving French Hill had not been called at the time of her post. — link

Circle Reports Q3 2026 Earnings: Revenue Up 17% to $865 Million, Average USDC Circulation Reaches $73.3 Billion Circle disclosed that revenue and reserve income in the third quarter of 2026 rose 17% year-over-year to $865 million, while net income from continuing operations increased 5% to $226 million. Other income included $182 million from the ARC token presale. During the period, the average circulating supply of USDC stood at $73.3 billion, up 8% year-over-year. Circle also stated that it has completed the genesis mint of 10 billion ARC tokens and signed a definitive agreement to acquire cross-border payments platform Tazapay. The transaction is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approval. Circle disclosed in its third-quarter 2026 earnings report that it reduced its workforce by approximately 5% during the quarter to better align its organizational structure with its operating model and strategic priorities. The restructuring resulted in approximately $9.15 million in charges, primarily related to severance payments, notice-period compensation, employee benefits, and associated costs. — link

Second-Largest Bitcoin Miner Riot Sells 10,599 BTC in Q3, Holdings Drop Nearly 79% from End of June Riot Platforms, the second-largest publicly listed Bitcoin mining company, sold 10,599 Bitcoin in the third quarter, reducing its holdings from 11,380 at the end of June to 2,418 at the end of September, a decline of nearly 79%. In the first nine months of the year, Riot sold a total of 20,264 BTC for approximately $1.5 billion, primarily to fund data center construction. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $181 million, up 1% year-over-year, with net income of $4.03 million, compared with $104 million in the same period last year. Bitcoin mining revenue was $116 million, down about 28% year-over-year. Riot also signed a 15-year data center lease agreement with an unnamed leading AI lab for 910 MW of IT capacity, with an initial contract value of approximately $28 billion. The company has now contracted a total of 1,151 MW of data center capacity, with long-term contract revenue of about $38 billion. — link
